title.zh: 卷五十四 志第二十三: 樂志
title.raw: 卷五十四 志第二十三: 樂志 Volume 54 Treatises 24: Music

sentences.zh: 遼有國樂，有雅樂，有大樂，有散樂，有鐃歌、橫吹樂。

translations.literal: The Liao had state music, ritual music, great music, miscellaneous music, nao songs, and horizontal-flute music.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao possessed state music, court ritual music, great music, popular miscellaneous music, nao drum songs, and horizontal-flute music.

sentences.zh: 舊史稱聖宗、興宗咸通音律，聲氣、歌辭、舞節，徵諸太常、儀鳳、教坊不可得。

translations.literal: Old histories say that Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong were thoroughly versed in pitch and rhythm, but sounds and airs, song texts, and dance measures—sought from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Office of Ceremonial Phoenixes, and the Training Bureau—could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories report that Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong were fully conversant with pitch and rhythm, yet the timbres, lyrics, and dance patterns could not be recovered from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Office of Ceremonial Phoenixes, or the Training Bureau.

sentences.zh: 按《紀》、《志》、《遼朝雜禮》，參考史籍，定其可知者，以補一代之闕文。

translations.literal: According to the Annals, Treatises, and Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty, consulting historical records, I fix what can be known to fill the lacunae of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the annals, treatises, and Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao, and consulting other historical sources, I have set down what can be established, to repair the gaps left in the record of that dynasty.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 《咸》、《韶》、《夏》、《武》之樂，聲亡書逸，河間作《記》，史遷因以為《書》，寥乎希哉，遼之樂，觀此足矣。

translations.literal: The music of Xian, Shao, Xia, and Wu—the sounds are lost and the books scattered; He Jian composed a Record, and Sima Qian took it as a Book—how sparse and rare! For Liao music, to view this suffices.
translations.idiomatic: The music of Xian, Shao, Xia, and Wu has vanished in sound and scattered in text; the Lord of Hejian compiled a Record, and Sima Qian treated it as a Classic—how remote and rare that is! For the music of the Liao, what is set down here is enough to judge by.

sentences.zh: ○國樂

translations.literal: ● State Music
translations.idiomatic: State Music

sentences.zh: 遼有國樂，猶先王之風；

translations.literal: The Liao had state music, like the airs of the former kings;
translations.idiomatic: The Liao had state music, comparable to the royal airs of antiquity;

sentences.zh: 其諸國樂，猶諸侯之風。

translations.literal: its music of the various states, like the airs of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: and the music of its subject peoples, comparable to the regional airs of the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 故誌其略。

translations.literal: Therefore its outline is recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Hence an outline is recorded here.

sentences.zh: 正月朔日朝賀，用宮懸雅樂。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month for court congratulation, suspended ritual music was used.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when the court offered congratulations, full suspended ritual music was performed.

sentences.zh: 元會，用大樂；

translations.literal: At the New Year assembly, great music was used;
translations.idiomatic: At the great New Year assembly, great music was used;

sentences.zh: 曲破後，用散樂；

translations.literal: after the suite-break, miscellaneous music was used;
translations.idiomatic: after the suite-break pieces, miscellaneous music was used;

sentences.zh: 角觝終之。

translations.literal: wrestling concluded it.
translations.idiomatic: and wrestling brought the program to a close.

sentences.zh: 是夜，皇帝燕飲，用國樂。

translations.literal: That night, at the emperor's banquet, state music was used.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, at the emperor's convivial feast, state music was performed.

sentences.zh: 七月十三日，皇帝出行宮三十里卓帳。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the seventh month, the emperor went thirty li from the travelling palace and pitched a tent.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the seventh month, the emperor rode thirty li from the travelling palace and set up camp in a great tent.

sentences.zh: 十四日設宴，應從諸軍隨各部落動樂。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth a feast was set; the various armies that accompanied him each raised music according to their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth a banquet was held, and each of the attendant armies played music according to its tribe.

sentences.zh: 十五日中元，大宴，用漢樂。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth, the Zhongyuan festival, a grand feast used Han music.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth, the Ghost Festival, a great banquet was held with Han music.

sentences.zh: 春飛放杏堝，皇帝射獲頭鵝，薦廟燕飲，樂工數十人執小樂器侑酒。

translations.literal: In spring at the apricot-marsh hunt, when the emperor shot and took the first goose, offerings were made at the temple and a banquet held; several dozen musicians held small instruments to ply the wine.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, when the hunt was opened at Apricot Marsh, the emperor shot the first goose; after offerings at the temple and a convivial feast, several dozen musicians played small instruments to accompany the toasts.

sentences.zh: 諸國樂

translations.literal: Music of the Various States
translations.idiomatic: Music of the Subject Peoples

sentences.zh: 太宗會同三年，晉宣徽使楊端、王朓等及諸國使朝見，皇帝御便殿賜宴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huitong, Emperor Taizong—when Jin Palace Secretariat commissioners Yang Duan, Wang Tuo, and others with envoys from various states came to audience—the emperor held a feast in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huitong, when Jin commissioners of the Palace Secretariat Yang Duan, Wang Tuo, and others came to court together with envoys from various states, Emperor Taizong received them in the side hall and granted a banquet.

sentences.zh: 朓起進酒，作歌舞，上為舉觴極歡。

translations.literal: Tuo rose to offer wine, performed song and dance; the emperor raised his cup in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tuo rose to present wine and performed songs and dances; the emperor raised his cup and rejoiced to the full.

sentences.zh: 會同三年端午日，百僚及諸國使稱賀，如式燕飲，命回鶻、敦煌二使作本國舞。

translations.literal: On the Dragon Boat Festival of the third year of Huitong, the hundred officials and envoys from various states offered congratulations; a banquet was held as prescribed, and the envoys of the Uyghurs and Dunhuang were ordered to perform their native dances.
translations.idiomatic: On the Dragon Boat Festival in the third year of Huitong, the officials and envoys from various states offered congratulations; a banquet was held according to ritual, and the Uyghur and Dunhuang envoys were commanded to perform the dances of their own countries.

sentences.zh: 天祚天慶二年，駕幸混同江，頭魚酒筵，半酣，上命諸酋長次第歌舞為樂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqing, Emperor Tianzuo visited the Huntong River; at the head-fish wine feast, when half drunk, the emperor ordered the various chieftains to sing and dance in turn for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqing, Emperor Tianzuo visited the Huntong River; at the head-fish banquet, when the wine had gone halfway, he ordered the chieftains to sing and dance in turn for entertainment.

sentences.zh: 女直阿骨打端立直視，辭以不能。

translations.literal: The Jurchen Aguda stood straight and stared directly; he declined on grounds of inability.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen leader Aguda stood erect and looked straight ahead, declining on the ground that he could not perform.

sentences.zh: 上謂蕭奉先曰：「阿骨打意氣雄豪，顧視不常，可托以邊事誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xiao Fengxian: "Aguda's spirit is bold and proud, his glances are not ordinary—he may be entrusted with frontier affairs and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Xiao Fengxian, "Aguda's bearing is bold and proud, and his gaze is unsettled. Find a pretext on the frontier and have him killed.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐貽後患。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I fear he will be a future trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear he will become a trouble for us later."

sentences.zh: 」奉先奏：「阿骨打無大過，殺之傷向化之意。

translations.literal: Fengxian memorialized: "Aguda has no great fault; to kill him would harm the intent to draw others to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxian replied, "Aguda has committed no serious offense. To kill him would wound our policy of winning others to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 蕞爾小國，又何能為。」

translations.literal: How could a petty little state do anything?"
translations.idiomatic: What harm can such a tiny state possibly do?"

sentences.zh: 聖宗太平元年，尊號冊禮，設宮懸於殿庭，舉麾位在殿第三重西階之上，協律郎各人就舉麾位，太常博士引太常卿，太常卿引皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Emperor Shengzong, at the ceremony for the honorific title, suspended bells were set in the palace courtyard; the baton positions were on the west steps of the third tier of the hall; each pitch-tuning officer took his baton position; Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the Director, the Director led the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping, at Emperor Shengzong's ceremony for the bestowal of an honorific title, full suspended bells were installed in the palace courtyard. The baton stations stood on the west steps of the hall's third tier; each pitch-tuning officer took his station; a Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, and the Director led the emperor.

sentences.zh: 將仗動，協律郎舉麾，太樂令令撞黃鐘之鐘，左右鐘皆應。

translations.literal: When the insignia were about to move, the pitch-tuning officer raised the baton; the Director of Music ordered the yellow-bell bell struck, and the bells left and right all responded.
translations.idiomatic: As the insignia were about to move, the pitch-tuning officer raised his baton; the Director of Music ordered the yellow-bell bell struck, and the bells on both sides answered.

sentences.zh: 工人舉，樂作；

translations.literal: The musicians raised [their instruments], music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: The musicians raised their instruments and the music began;

sentences.zh: 皇帝即御坐，扇合，樂止。

translations.literal: the emperor took the imperial seat, fans were folded, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor took the throne, the fans were closed, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 王公入門，樂作；

translations.literal: When princes and dukes entered the gate, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: When princes and dukes entered the gate, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 至位，樂止。

translations.literal: when they reached position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when they reached their places, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引押冊大臣初動，樂作；

translations.literal: The protocol officer led the minister escorting the register at the first movement, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officer led the minister bearing the document of investiture at the first movement, and music sounded;

sentences.zh: 置冊殿前香案訖，就位，樂止。

translations.literal: when the register was placed on the incense table before the hall and they took position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the document had been set on the incense table before the hall and they had taken their places, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 舁冊官奉冊，初動，樂作；

translations.literal: The officers bearing the register presented it; at the first movement, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: The officers carrying the document of investiture presented it; at the first movement, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 升殿，置冊御坐前，就西墉北上位，樂止。

translations.literal: they ascended the hall, placed the register before the imperial seat, and took position north of the west parapet; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: they ascended the hall, set the document before the throne, and took their places north of the west parapet; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 大臣上殿，樂作；

translations.literal: When the minister ascended the hall, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: When the minister ascended the hall, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 至殿欄內位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he reached position inside the hall railing, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when he reached his place inside the hall railing, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 大臣降殿階，樂作；

translations.literal: When the minister descended the hall steps, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: When the minister descended the hall steps, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 復位，樂止。

translations.literal: when he returned to position, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when he returned to his place, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 王公三品以上出，樂作；

translations.literal: When princes and dukes of the third rank and above departed, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: When princes and dukes of the third rank and above withdrew, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 太常博士引太常卿，太常卿引皇帝降御坐入閣，樂止。

translations.literal: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, the Director led the emperor down from the imperial seat into the side chamber; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, and the Director led the emperor down from the throne into the side chamber; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 興宗重熙九年，上契丹冊，皇帝出，奏《隆安》之樂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongxi, Emperor Xingzong, at the presentation of the Khitan register, when the emperor came forth, the music "Long Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chongxi, when the Khitan document of investiture was presented, the music Long Peace was played as the emperor came forth.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子儀：太子初入門，《貞安》之樂作。

translations.literal: Ceremony for investing the crown prince: when the crown prince first entered the gate, the music "Upright Peace" sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for investing the crown prince: when the crown prince first entered the gate, the music Upright Peace was performed.

sentences.zh: 冊禮樂工次第：四隅各置建鼓一虡，樂工各一人；

translations.literal: Order of musicians at the investiture ceremony: at each of the four corners one set of establishment drums was placed, one musician each;
translations.idiomatic: Order of musicians at the investiture ceremony: at each of the four corners one rack of establishment drums was set up, with one musician at each;

sentences.zh: 宮懸每面九虡，每虡樂工一人；

translations.literal: on each side of the suspended bells nine racks, one musician per rack;
translations.idiomatic: on each side of the suspended orchestra nine racks, with one musician at each rack;

sentences.zh: 樂虡近北置、各一，樂工各一人；

translations.literal: near the north of each music rack one [rack] was placed, one musician each;
translations.idiomatic: one additional rack placed near the north of each music stand, with one musician at each;

sentences.zh: 樂虡內坐部樂工，左右各一百二人；

translations.literal: within the music racks, seated-section musicians, one hundred two on the left and right each;
translations.idiomatic: within the music stands, seated-section musicians numbered one hundred and two on the left and on the right;

sentences.zh: 樂虡西南武舞六十四人，執小旗二人；

translations.literal: southwest of the music racks, military dancers sixty-four, two bearing small banners;
translations.idiomatic: southwest of the music stands, sixty-four military dancers, with two bearing small banners;

sentences.zh: 樂虡東南文舞六十四人，執小旗二人；

translations.literal: southeast of the music racks, civil dancers sixty-four, two bearing small banners;
translations.idiomatic: southeast of the music stands, sixty-four civil dancers, with two bearing small banners;

sentences.zh: 協律郎二人；

translations.literal: pitch-tuning officers two;
translations.idiomatic: two pitch-tuning officers;

sentences.zh: 太樂令一人。

translations.literal: Director of Music one.
translations.idiomatic: one Director of Music.

sentences.zh: 唐《十二和》樂，遼初用之，《豫和》祀天神，《順和》祭地祗，《永和》享宗廟，《肅和》登歌奠玉帛，《雍和》入俎接神，《壽和》酌獻飲神，《太和》節升降，《舒和》節出入，《昭和》舉酒，《休和》以飯，《正和》皇后受冊以行，《承和》太子以行。

translations.literal: The Tang Twelve Harmonies music was used at the beginning of the Liao: Yuhe for sacrificing to Heaven, Shunhe for sacrificing to Earth, Yonghe for enjoying the ancestral temple, Suhe for ascending to sing and presenting jade and silk, Yonghe for entering the stand and receiving the spirit, Shouhe for pouring libation and drinking to the spirit, Taihe for regulating ascent and descent, Shuhe for regulating entry and exit, Zhaohe for raising wine, Xiuhe for eating, Zhenghe for the empress receiving the register in procession, Chenghe for the crown prince in procession.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Twelve Harmonies were used in the early Liao: Yuhe when sacrificing to Heaven, Shunhe to Earth, Yonghe in the ancestral temple, Suhe when ascending to sing and presenting jade and silk, Yonghe when the offering entered the stand to receive the spirit, Shouhe for libation and drinking to the spirit, Taihe to regulate ascent and descent, Shuhe to regulate entry and exit, Zhaohe when wine was raised, Xiuhe at the meal, Zhenghe when the empress received the register in procession, and Chenghe when the crown prince went in procession.

sentences.zh: 遼《十二安》樂：初，梁改唐《十二和》樂為《九慶》樂，後唐建唐宗廟，仍用《十二和》樂，晉改為《十二同》樂。

translations.literal: The Liao Twelve Tranquilities music: at first Liang changed the Tang Twelve Harmonies to Nine Celebrations; Later Tang built the Tang ancestral temple and still used the Twelve Harmonies; Jin changed them to the Twelve Unities.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao Twelve Tranquilities: at first the Liang had changed the Tang Twelve Harmonies to Nine Celebrations; Later Tang, when it built the Tang ancestral temple, reverted to the Twelve Harmonies; Jin renamed them the Twelve Unities.

sentences.zh: 《遼雜禮》「天子出入，奏《隆安》；

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao state: "When the Son of Heaven enters or exits, perform Long Peace;
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao records: "When the Son of Heaven enters or exits, perform Long Peace;

sentences.zh: 太子行，奏《貞安》」，則是遼嘗改樂名矣。

translations.literal: when the crown prince goes in procession, perform Upright Peace"—thus the Liao did change music names.
translations.idiomatic: when the crown prince goes in procession, perform Upright Peace"—which shows that the Liao did rename some pieces.

sentences.zh: 餘十安樂名缺。

translations.literal: The names of the remaining ten Tranquilities are missing.
translations.idiomatic: The names of the remaining ten Tranquilities are lost.

sentences.zh: 遼雅樂歌辭，文闕不具；

translations.literal: The song texts of Liao ritual music are incomplete in the text;
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics of Liao ritual music survive only in fragmentary form;

sentences.zh: 八音器數，大抵因唐之舊。

translations.literal: the numbers of the eight categories of instruments largely follow Tang usage.
translations.idiomatic: but the roster of instruments in the eight categories largely follows Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 八音：金縛、鐘石球、磬

translations.literal: Eight categories: metal—bind and fou; stone—bells, sphere, and qing.
translations.idiomatic: The eight categories: metal—gongs and cymbals; stone—bells, sounding stones, and chime-stones.

sentences.zh: 絲琴、瑟竹籥、簫、竾匏笙、竽土籥

translations.literal: silk—qin and se; bamboo—yue, xiao, and chi; gourd—sheng and yu; earth—yue.
translations.idiomatic: silk—the qin and se zithers; bamboo—the yue pipe, xiao flute, and chi; gourd—the sheng and yu mouth-organs; earth—the ocarina.

sentences.zh: 革鼓、鼗木、

translations.literal: leather—drum and tambourine; wood—
translations.idiomatic: leather—drums and tambourines; wood—

sentences.zh: 十二律用周黍尺九寸管，空徑三分為本。

translations.literal: The twelve pitch pipes used the Zhou millet-measure nine-inch tube, with an empty diameter of three fen as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pitch pipes were based on the Zhou millet-measure: a nine-inch tube with an inner diameter of three fen.

sentences.zh: 道宗大康中，詔行黍所定升斗，嘗定律矣。

translations.literal: In the Dakang era of Emperor Daozong, an edict ordered the use of the bushel and peck fixed by the millet measure, and pitch was once regulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dakang era of Emperor Daozong, an edict ordered the adoption of the bushel and peck defined by the millet measure, and the pitch standard was once fixed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其法大抵用古律焉。

translations.literal: Its method largely employed the ancient pitch standard.
translations.idiomatic: The method employed was largely that of the ancient pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 大樂

translations.literal: Great Music
translations.idiomatic: Great Music

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，因秦、楚之聲置樂府。

translations.literal: From Han onward, on the basis of Qin and Chu sounds the Music Bureau was established.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, a Music Bureau was established to preserve the sounds of Qin and Chu.

sentences.zh: 至隋高祖詔求知音者，鄭譯得西域蘇祗婆七旦之聲，求合七音八十四調之說，由是雅俗之樂，皆此聲矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Sui Gaozu's edict seeking those who knew music, Zheng Yi obtained from the Western Regions the seven-mode sounds of Kuchean Sujiva, seeking to match the theory of seven tones and eighty-four modes; henceforth ritual and popular music alike were all this sound.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Gaozu issued an edict seeking masters of music, Zheng Yi obtained from the Western Regions the seven-mode system of the Kuchean musician Sujiva and sought to align it with the theory of seven tones and eighty-four modes; from that point, both court ritual and popular music drew on these sounds.

sentences.zh: 用之朝廷，別於雅樂者，謂之大樂。

translations.literal: Used at court, distinct from ritual music, it was called great music.
translations.idiomatic: What was used at court and distinguished from ritual music was called great music.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖使馮道、劉煦冊應天太后、太宗皇帝，其聲器、工官與法駕，同歸於遼。

translations.literal: Jin Gaozu sent Feng Dao and Liu Xu to invest Empress Dowager Yingtian and Emperor Taizong; their musical instruments, artisan officials, and imperial regalia all passed together to the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu sent Feng Dao and Liu Xu to invest Empress Dowager Yingtian and Emperor Taizong, the musical instruments, musicians, and imperial regalia all passed into Liao hands together.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和元年，冊承天皇太后，童子弟子隊樂引太后輦至金鑾門。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tonghe, Emperor Shengzong, at the investiture of Empress Dowager Chengtian, the boy-disciple corps music led the empress dowager's carriage to the Golden Phoenix Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tonghe, when Empress Dowager Chengtian was invested, the boy-disciple musical corps escorted the empress dowager's carriage with music to the Golden Phoenix Gate.

sentences.zh: 天祚皇帝天慶元年上壽儀：皇帝出東閣，鳴鞭，樂作；

translations.literal: Ceremony for offering long life, first year of Tianqing, Emperor Tianzuo: the emperor came forth from the east side chamber, the whip was sounded, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony for offering long life in the first year of Tianqing, Emperor Tianzuo: the emperor came forth from the east side chamber, the whip was sounded, and music began;

sentences.zh: 簾卷，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: the curtains were rolled up, fans opened, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the curtains were raised, the fans opened, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 太尉執臺，分班，太樂令舉麾，樂作；

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant held the goblet-stand, ranks were divided; the Director of Music raised the baton, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant held the goblet-stand and the officials took their ranks; the Director of Music raised his baton and music sounded;

sentences.zh: 皇帝飲酒訖，樂止。

translations.literal: when the emperor finished drinking, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor had finished drinking, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 應坐臣僚東西外殿，太樂令引堂上，樂升。

translations.literal: The officials who should be seated in the east and west outer halls—the Director of Music led them onto the hall platform; music rose.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who were to be seated in the east and west outer halls were led onto the hall platform by the Director of Music as the music swelled.

sentences.zh: 大臣執臺，太樂令奏舉觴，登歌，樂作；

translations.literal: The minister held the goblet-stand; the Director of Music announced raising the cup; ascending song; music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: A minister held the goblet-stand; the Director of Music announced the raising of the cup; the ascending song was performed and music sounded;

sentences.zh: 飲訖，樂止。

translations.literal: when drinking was finished, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the drinking was finished, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 行臣僚酒遍，太樂令奏巡周，舉麾，樂作；

translations.literal: When the round of wine for the officials was completed, the Director of Music announced the circuit round, raised the baton, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: When wine had been passed to all the officials, the Director of Music announced the circuit round, raised his baton, and music sounded;

sentences.zh: 飲訖，樂止。

translations.literal: when drinking was finished, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the drinking was finished, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常卿進禦食，太樂令奏食遍，樂作；

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented the imperial food; the Director of Music announced the food round complete, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented the imperial meal; the Director of Music announced that the food round was complete, and music sounded;

sentences.zh: 《文舞》入，三變，引出，樂止。

translations.literal: the Civil Dance entered, three changes, then led out; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the Civil Dance entered, performed three changes, and was led out; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次進酒，行臣僚酒，舉觴，巡周，樂作；

translations.literal: Next wine was presented; wine was passed among the officials, cups raised, circuit round; music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: Next wine was presented and passed among the officials; cups were raised and the circuit round performed as music sounded;

sentences.zh: 飲訖，樂止。

translations.literal: when drinking was finished, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the drinking was finished, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次進食，食遍，樂作；

translations.literal: Next food was presented; when the food round was complete, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: Next food was presented; when the food round was complete, music sounded;

sentences.zh: 《武舞》入，三變，引出，樂止。

translations.literal: the Military Dance entered, three changes, then led out; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the Military Dance entered, performed three changes, and was led out; the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 扇合，簾下，鳴鞭樂作；

translations.literal: fans were folded, curtains lowered, the whip sounded, music sounded;
translations.idiomatic: the fans were closed, the curtains lowered, the whip was sounded, and music began;

sentences.zh: 皇帝入西閣，樂止。

translations.literal: the emperor entered the west side chamber; music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor entered the west side chamber and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 大樂器：本唐太宗《七德》、《九功》之樂。

translations.literal: Great-music instruments: originally the music of Emperor Taizong of Tang, the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments of great music: they originally belonged to Emperor Taizong of Tang's Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements suites.

sentences.zh: 武后毀唐宗廟，《七德》、《九功》樂舞遂亡，自後宗廟用隋《文》、《武》二舞。

translations.literal: Empress Wu destroyed the Tang ancestral temple, and the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements dances were lost; thereafter the ancestral temple used the Sui Civil and Military dances.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu destroyed the Tang ancestral temple, the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements dances were lost; thereafter the ancestral temple used the Sui Civil and Military dances.

sentences.zh: 朝廷用高宗《景雲》樂代之，元會，第一奏《景雲》樂舞。

translations.literal: At court Emperor Gaozong's Jingyun music replaced them; at the New Year assembly, the Jingyun dance was performed first.
translations.idiomatic: At court they were replaced by Emperor Gaozong's Jingyun music; at the New Year assembly the Jingyun dance was performed first.

sentences.zh: 杜佑《通典》已稱諸樂並亡。

translations.literal: Du You's Comprehensive Institutions already stated that all these pieces were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Du You's Comprehensive Institutions already records that all these pieces were lost.

sentences.zh: 唯《景雲》樂舞僅存。

translations.literal: Only the Jingyun dance barely survived.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Jingyun dance barely survived.

sentences.zh: 唐末、五代板蕩之餘，在者希矣。

translations.literal: After the turmoil of late Tang and the Five Dynasties, what remained was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: After the upheavals of late Tang and the Five Dynasties, little survived.

sentences.zh: 遼國大樂，晉代所傳。

translations.literal: The great music of the Liao state was transmitted from the Jin dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The great music of the Liao was what had been transmitted from the Jin.

sentences.zh: 雜禮雖見坐部樂工左右各一百二人，蓋亦以《景雲》遺工充坐部；

translations.literal: Although the Miscellaneous Rites mention seated-section musicians, one hundred two on the left and right each, presumably survivors of Jingyun filled the seated section;
translations.idiomatic: Although the Miscellaneous Rites mention one hundred and two seated-section musicians on the left and right, they were presumably filled by surviving practitioners of Jingyun;

sentences.zh: 其坐、立部樂，自唐已亡，可考者唯《景雲》四部樂舞而已。

translations.literal: the seated and standing sections of music had been lost since Tang; what can be verified is only the four-section Jingyun dance.
translations.idiomatic: the seated and standing sections of music had been lost since the Tang; all that can be verified is the four-part Jingyun dance alone.

sentences.zh: 玉磬方響搊箏築

translations.literal: jade chimes, fangxiang sounding plates, pipa, zheng, and zhu.
translations.idiomatic: jade chimes, metal sounding plates, pipa lute, zheng zither, and stick-zither.

sentences.zh: 臥箜篌大箜篌小箜篌大琵琶

translations.literal: reclining konghou, large konghou, small konghou, large pipa
translations.idiomatic: reclining konghou, large konghou, small konghou, and large pipa

sentences.zh: 小琵琶大五弦小五弦吹葉

translations.literal: small pipa, large five-string, small five-string, leaf-blowing
translations.idiomatic: small pipa, large five-string lute, small five-string lute, and leaf-whistling

sentences.zh: 大笙小笙觱篥簫

translations.literal: large sheng, small sheng, bili, xiao
translations.idiomatic: large sheng, small sheng, bili pipe, and xiao flute

sentences.zh: 銅鈸長笛尺八笛短笛

translations.literal: bronze cymbals, long flute, shakuhachi flute, short flute
translations.idiomatic: bronze cymbals, long flute, shakuhachi flute, and short flute

sentences.zh: 以上皆一人。

translations.literal: for all the above, one person each.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the above was played by one musician.

sentences.zh: 毛員鼓連鼗鼓貝

translations.literal: Mao-yuan drum, linked tambourine drums, shell
translations.idiomatic: Mao-yuan drum, linked tambourines, and conch shell

sentences.zh: 以上皆二人，余每器工一人。

translations.literal: for all the above, two persons each; for the rest, one artisan per instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the above required two musicians; for the remaining instruments, one player per instrument.

sentences.zh: 歌二人。

translations.literal: singers two.
translations.idiomatic: There were two singers.

sentences.zh: 舞二十人，分四部：《景雲》舞八人

translations.literal: dancers twenty, divided into four sections: Jingyun dance eight persons
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty dancers, divided into four sections: eight for the Jingyun dance

sentences.zh: 《慶雲》樂舞四人《破陣》樂舞四人《承天》樂舞四人

translations.literal: Qingyun music-dance four persons, Pozhen music-dance four persons, Chengtian music-dance four persons
translations.idiomatic: four for the Qingyun dance, four for the Pozhen dance, and four for the Chengtian dance

sentences.zh: 大樂調：雅樂有七音，大樂亦有七聲，謂之七旦：一曰娑陁力，平聲；

translations.literal: Great-music modes: ritual music has seven tones; great music also has seven sounds, called the seven modes: first, Satuoli, level tone;
translations.idiomatic: Modes of great music: ritual music has seven tones, and great music likewise has seven sounds, called the seven modes. The first is Satuoli, the level tone;

sentences.zh: 二曰雞識，長聲；

translations.literal: second, Jishi, long tone;
translations.idiomatic: the second is Jishi, the long tone;

sentences.zh: 三曰沙識，質直聲；

translations.literal: third, Shashi, straightforward tone;
translations.idiomatic: the third is Shashi, the straightforward tone;

sentences.zh: 四曰沙侯加濫，應聲；

translations.literal: fourth, Shahou jialan, responding tone;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth is Shahou jialan, the responding tone;

sentences.zh: 五曰沙臘，應和聲；

translations.literal: fifth, Shala, harmonizing tone;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth is Shala, the harmonizing tone;

sentences.zh: 六曰般贍，五聲；

translations.literal: sixth, Banshan, pentatonic tone;
translations.idiomatic: the sixth is Banshan, the pentatonic tone;

sentences.zh: 七曰俟利<辶筆>，斛牛聲。

translations.literal: seventh, Sili chan, the sound of a measuring ox.
translations.idiomatic: the seventh is Sili chan, the measuring-ox tone.

sentences.zh: 自隋以來，樂府取其聲，四旦二十八調為大樂。

translations.literal: From Sui onward, the Music Bureau took these sounds; four modes and twenty-eight keys constituted great music.
translations.idiomatic: From the Sui dynasty onward, the Music Bureau adopted these sounds; four modes and twenty-eight keys made up great music.

sentences.zh: 娑陁力旦：正宮高宮中呂宮

translations.literal: Satuoli mode: proper palace, high palace, central lü palace
translations.idiomatic: Satuoli mode: proper palace, high palace, and central lü palace

sentences.zh: 道調宮南呂宮仙呂宮黃鐘宮

translations.literal: dao-mode palace, southern lü palace, immortal lü palace, yellow-bell palace
translations.idiomatic: dao-mode palace, southern lü palace, immortal lü palace, and yellow-bell palace

sentences.zh: 雞識旦：越調大食調高大食調

translations.literal: Jishi mode: Yue mode, Great Food mode, High Great Food mode
translations.idiomatic: Jishi mode: Yue mode, Great Food mode, and High Great Food mode

sentences.zh: 雙調小食調歇指調林鐘商調

translations.literal: Double mode, Small Food mode, Resting Finger mode, Forest Bell merchant mode
translations.idiomatic: Double mode, Small Food mode, Resting Finger mode, and Forest Bell merchant mode

sentences.zh: 沙識旦：大食角高大食角雙角

translations.literal: Shashi mode: Great Food corner, High Great Food corner, Double corner
translations.idiomatic: Shashi mode: Great Food corner, High Great Food corner, and Double corner

sentences.zh: 小食角歇指角林鐘角越角

translations.literal: Small Food corner, Resting Finger corner, Forest Bell corner, Yue corner
translations.idiomatic: Small Food corner, Resting Finger corner, Forest Bell corner, and Yue corner

sentences.zh: 般涉旦：中呂調正平調高平調

translations.literal: Banshe mode: central lü mode, proper level mode, high level mode
translations.idiomatic: Banshe mode: central lü mode, proper level mode, and high level mode

sentences.zh: 仙呂調黃鐘調般涉調高般涉調

translations.literal: immortal lü mode, yellow-bell mode, banshe mode, high banshe mode
translations.idiomatic: immortal lü mode, yellow-bell mode, banshe mode, and high banshe mode

sentences.zh: 右四旦二十八調，不用黍律，以琵琶弦葉之。

translations.literal: The four modes and twenty-eight keys on the right do not use millet pitch pipes but take their standard from pipa strings.
translations.idiomatic: These four modes and twenty-eight keys did not use millet pitch pipes but were calibrated by the strings of the pipa.

sentences.zh: 皆從濁至清，叠更其聲，下益濁，上益清。

translations.literal: All proceed from muddy to clear, layering and changing their sounds; going down increases muddiness, going up increases clarity.
translations.idiomatic: All proceeded from low to high pitch, changing sound in layers: lowering made the tone muddier, raising made it clearer.

sentences.zh: 七七四十九調，餘二十一調失其傳。

translations.literal: Seven times seven is forty-nine modes; the remaining twenty-one modes lost their transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Seven times seven makes forty-nine modes; twenty-one of them have lost their transmission.

sentences.zh: 蓋出九部樂之《龜茲部》雲。

translations.literal: Presumably they come from the Kuche section of the nine-department music, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: They are said to derive from the Kuche section of the nine-department music.

sentences.zh: 大樂聲：各調之中，度曲協音，其聲凡十，曰：五、凡、工、尺、上、一、四、六、勾、合，近十二雅律，於律呂各闕其一，猶雅音之不及商也。

translations.literal: Great-music tones: within each mode, when setting melodies and harmonizing pitches, there are ten sounds in all, namely: wu, fan, gong, chi, shang, yi, si, liu, gou, he—close to the twelve ritual pitches, but each pitch class lacks one, just as ritual tone does not reach merchant tone.
translations.idiomatic: Tones of great music: within each mode, when melodies were set and pitches harmonized, there were ten sounds in all—wu, fan, gong, chi, shang, yi, si, liu, gou, and he—approximating the twelve ritual pitches yet lacking one from each class, much as ritual tone falls short of merchant tone.

sentences.zh: 散樂

translations.literal: Miscellaneous Music
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous Music

sentences.zh: 殷人作靡靡之樂，其聲往而不反，流為鄭、衛之聲。

translations.literal: The people of Yin made decadent music; its sound went forth and did not return, flowing into the sounds of Zheng and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin made decadent music whose sound went out and did not return, eventually flowing into the music of Zheng and Wei.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢之間，秦、楚聲作，鄭、衛浸亡。

translations.literal: Between Qin and Han, Qin and Chu sounds arose, and Zheng and Wei gradually perished.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Qin and Han dynasties, Qin and Chu sounds arose while Zheng and Wei music gradually died out.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝以李延年典樂府，稍用西涼之聲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han put Li Yannian in charge of the Music Bureau and gradually used Western Liang sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han placed Li Yannian in charge of the Music Bureau and gradually introduced sounds from Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 今之散樂，俳優、歌舞雜進，往往漢樂府之遺聲。

translations.literal: Today's miscellaneous music, with actors, song, and dance entering in mixture, is often the surviving sound of the Han Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Present-day miscellaneous music, with actors, songs, and dances presented in succession, often preserves sounds handed down from the Han Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，遣劉句以伶官來歸，遼有散樂，蓋由此矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin, Liu Gou was sent with entertainers to return; the Liao had miscellaneous music—presumably from this.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu, Jin sent Liu Gou back with court entertainers; the Liao acquired miscellaneous music, presumably from this event.

sentences.zh: 遼冊皇后儀：呈百戲、角觝、戲馬以為樂。

translations.literal: Liao ceremony for investing the empress: presenting the hundred entertainments, wrestling, and horse play as music.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liao ceremony for investing an empress, the hundred entertainments, wrestling, and horse play were presented as amusement.

sentences.zh: 皇帝生辰樂次：酒一行觱篥起，歌。

translations.literal: Order of music at the emperor's birthday: at the first round of wine, bili sounded and singing began.
translations.idiomatic: Order of music at the emperor's birthday: at the first round of wine, the bili sounded and singing began.

sentences.zh: 酒二行歌，手伎入。

translations.literal: At the second round of wine, singing; hand acrobats entered.
translations.idiomatic: At the second round of wine came singing, and hand acrobats entered.

sentences.zh: 酒三行琵琶獨彈。

translations.literal: At the third round of wine, pipa solo.
translations.idiomatic: At the third round of wine, a solo on the pipa.

sentences.zh: 餅、茶、致語。

translations.literal: cakes, tea, formal address.
translations.idiomatic: Cakes, tea, and formal address.

sentences.zh: 食入，雜劇進。

translations.literal: food entered; miscellaneous plays advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Food was served and miscellaneous plays were presented.

sentences.zh: 酒四行闕。

translations.literal: At the fourth round of wine, omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth round of wine was omitted.

sentences.zh: 酒五行笙獨吹，鼓笛進。

translations.literal: At the fifth round of wine, sheng solo; drums and flutes advanced.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth round of wine, a solo on the sheng, and drums and flutes entered.

sentences.zh: 酒六行箏獨彈，築球。

translations.literal: At the sixth round of wine, zheng solo; zhu and ball.
translations.idiomatic: At the sixth round of wine, a solo on the zheng, then stick-zither and ball games.

sentences.zh: 酒七行歌曲破，角觝。

translations.literal: At the seventh round of wine, song suite-break and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: At the seventh round of wine came song suite-break pieces and wrestling.

sentences.zh: 曲宴宋國使樂次：

translations.literal: Order of music at a private banquet for the Song envoy:
translations.idiomatic: Order of music at a private banquet for the Song envoy:

sentences.zh: 酒一行觱篥起，歌。

translations.literal: At the first round of wine, bili sounded and singing began.
translations.idiomatic: At the first round of wine, the bili sounded and singing began.

sentences.zh: 酒二行歌。

translations.literal: At the second round of wine, singing.
translations.idiomatic: At the second round of wine came singing.

sentences.zh: 酒三行歌，手伎入。

translations.literal: At the third round of wine, singing; hand acrobats entered.
translations.idiomatic: At the third round of wine came singing, and hand acrobats entered.

sentences.zh: 酒四行琵琶獨彈。

translations.literal: At the fourth round of wine, pipa solo.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth round of wine, a solo on the pipa.

sentences.zh: 餅、茶、致語。

translations.literal: cakes, tea, formal address.
translations.idiomatic: Cakes, tea, and formal address.

sentences.zh: 食入，雜劇進。

translations.literal: food entered; miscellaneous plays advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Food was served and miscellaneous plays were presented.

sentences.zh: 酒五行闕。

translations.literal: At the fifth round of wine, omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth round of wine was omitted.

sentences.zh: 酒六行笙獨吹，合《法曲》。

translations.literal: At the sixth round of wine, sheng solo, performing the Legal Suite.
translations.idiomatic: At the sixth round of wine came a solo on the sheng, performing the Legal Suite.

sentences.zh: 酒七行箏獨彈。

translations.literal: At the seventh round of wine, zheng solo.
translations.idiomatic: At the seventh round of wine, a solo on the zheng.

sentences.zh: 酒八行歌，擊架樂。

translations.literal: At the eighth round of wine, singing and frame-drumming music.
translations.idiomatic: At the eighth round of wine came singing and music on the frame drums.

sentences.zh: 酒九行歌，角觝。

translations.literal: At the ninth round of wine, singing and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: At the ninth round of wine came singing and wrestling.

sentences.zh: 散樂，以三音該三才之義，四聲調四時之氣，應十二管之數。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous music, with three tones encompassing the meaning of the three powers, four sounds regulating the qi of the four seasons, corresponding to the number of the twelve pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous music used three tones to encompass the three powers, four sounds to regulate the four seasons, and corresponded to the number of the twelve pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 截竹為四竅之笛，以葉音聲，而被之弦歌。

translations.literal: Bamboo was cut to make four-hole flutes; with leaf-tones as sound, string songs were laid over them.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo was cut into four-hole flutes; leaf-tones provided the pitch, and string songs were performed to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 三音：天音揚，地音抑，人音中，皆有聲無文。

translations.literal: Three tones: heaven-tone rises, earth-tone falls, human-tone is central—all have sound without text.
translations.idiomatic: The three tones were heaven-tone rising, earth-tone falling, and human-tone in the middle—all sound without written text.

sentences.zh: 四時：春聲曰平，夏聲曰上，秋聲曰去，冬聲曰入。

translations.literal: Four seasons: spring-sound is called level, summer-sound rising, autumn-sound departing, winter-sound entering.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons were represented in sound: spring as level tone, summer as rising, autumn as departing, and winter as entering.

sentences.zh: 散樂器：觱篥、簫、笛、笙、琵琶、五弦、箜篌、箏、方響、杖鼓、第二鼓、第三鼓、腰鼓、大鼓、鞚、拍板。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous-music instruments: bili, xiao, flute, sheng, pipa, five-string, konghou, zheng, fangxiang, staff drum, second drum, third drum, waist drum, large drum, kong drum, clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments of miscellaneous music included the bili, xiao, flute, sheng, pipa, five-string lute, konghou, zheng, metal sounding plates, staff drum, second drum, third drum, waist drum, large drum, kong drum, and clappers.

sentences.zh: 雜戲：自齊景公用倡優侏儒，至漢武帝設魚龍曼延之戲，後漢有繩舞、自刳之伎，杜佑以為多幻術，皆出西域。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous entertainments: from Duke Jing of Qi's use of actors and dwarfs, to Emperor Wu of Han's fish-dragon spreading play, Later Han had rope dance and self-disemboweling acts—Du You considered most of these illusion arts, all coming from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous entertainments: from Duke Jing of Qi's actors and dwarfs to Emperor Wu of Han's fish-dragon pageant, and in Later Han rope dances and self-disemboweling acts—Du You regarded most of these as illusion arts originating in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 哇俚不經，故不具述。

translations.literal: vulgar and unorthodox, therefore not fully described.
translations.idiomatic: They are vulgar and unorthodox, and so are not described in full.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹樂

translations.literal: Drum-and-wind Music
translations.idiomatic: Drum-and-Wind Music

sentences.zh: 鼓吹樂，一曰短簫鐃歌樂，自漢有之，謂之軍樂。

translations.literal: Drum-and-wind music, also called short-flute nao-song music, has existed since Han and is called military music.
translations.idiomatic: Drum-and-wind music, also called short-flute nao-song music, has existed since the Han and is known as military music.

sentences.zh: 《遼雜禮》，朝會設熊羆十二案，法駕有前後部鼓吹，百官鹵簿皆有鼓吹樂。

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao: at court assemblies twelve bear-and-panther tables were set; the imperial regalia had front and rear drum-and-wind sections; every official's guard of honor had drum-and-wind music.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao, court assemblies set out twelve bear-and-panther tables; the imperial procession had front and rear drum-and-wind sections; and every official's guard of honor included drum-and-wind music.

sentences.zh: 前部：

translations.literal: Front section:
translations.idiomatic: Front section:

sentences.zh: 簫二十四笳二十四右前後鼓吹，行則導駕奏之，朝會則列仗，設而不奏。

translations.literal: xiao twenty-four, qiang twenty-four. The front and rear drum-and-wind on the right: when travelling they led the carriage and played; at court assemblies they were drawn up in formation, set out but not played.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-four xiao and twenty-four qiang. The front and rear drum-and-wind sections: when the emperor travelled they led the procession and played; at court assemblies they were drawn up in formation but set out without being played.

sentences.zh: 橫吹樂

translations.literal: Horizontal-Flute Music
translations.idiomatic: Horizontal-Flute Music

sentences.zh: 橫吹亦軍樂，與鼓吹分部而同用，皆屬鼓吹令。

translations.literal: Horizontal-flute music is also military music; it is a separate section from drum-and-wind but used together, all under the Director of drum-and-wind.
translations.idiomatic: Horizontal-flute music is also military music; though organized separately from drum-and-wind, it was used together with it, all under the Director of drum-and-wind.

translations.idiomatic: twenty-four xiao, twenty-four bili, twenty-four peach-skin qian-bili

sentences.zh: 百官鼓吹、橫吹樂，自四品以上，各有增損，見《儀衛志》。

translations.literal: Drum-and-wind and horizontal-flute music for the hundred officials, from the fourth rank upward, each had additions or reductions—see the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The drum-and-wind and horizontal-flute music allotted to officials of the fourth rank and above varied in scale; see the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.

sentences.zh: 自周衰，先王之樂浸以亡缺，《周南》變為《秦風》。

translations.literal: From the decline of Zhou, the music of the former kings gradually perished and was lost; the Odes of Zhou and the South changed into the Airs of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: From the decline of Zhou onward, the music of the former kings gradually vanished; the Odes of Zhou and the South gave way to the Airs of Qin.

sentences.zh: 始皇有天下，鄭、衛、秦、燕、趙、楚之聲叠進，而雅聲亡矣。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor possessed the realm, the sounds of Zheng, Wei, Qin, Yan, Zhao, and Chu advanced in layers, and ritual sound perished.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor united the realm, the sounds of Zheng, Wei, Qin, Yan, Zhao, and Chu crowded in one after another, and ritual music was lost.

sentences.zh: 漢唐之盛，文事多西音，是為大樂、散樂；

translations.literal: At the height of Han and Tang, civil affairs mostly used western sounds—this is great music and miscellaneous music;
translations.idiomatic: At the height of Han and Tang, civil ceremonies drew heavily on western sounds—this is great music and miscellaneous music;

sentences.zh: 武事皆北音，是為鼓吹、橫吹樂。

translations.literal: military affairs all used northern sounds—this is drum-and-wind and horizontal-flute music.
translations.idiomatic: military affairs relied on northern sounds—this is drum-and-wind and horizontal-flute music.

sentences.zh: 雅樂在者，其器雅，其音亦西雲。

translations.literal: Of ritual music that survives, its instruments are refined, but its sound is also western, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: What survives of ritual music has refined instruments, yet its sound too is said to be western in character.
